issues.title: Incorrect Case A column normalization

failure_location.quote: Multiplying its first column by $t = \frac{1}{1 - b^2} > 1$ we get the orthogonal matrix

issues.failure_explanation: Because B has orthonormal columns and its first row is (b,0), the two columns of C are orthogonal with squared norms 1-b^2 and 1. With the printed t=1/(1-b^2), the scaled first column has squared norm 1/(1-b^2), not 1, and 1/t^2=(1-b^2)^2 rather than 1-b^2. Thus the induction hypothesis for orthonormal columns and the calculation in ineq are invalid.
issues.overall_effect: The Case A induction step does not establish the proposition's bound or strictness, leaving pr and its polygonal corollary unproved until the normalization is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Case A definition by t=(1-b²)^(-1/2) and retain the construction Ć=C·diag(t,1). Then Ć has orthonormal columns and t^(-2)=1-b², so the induction, bound, strictness analysis, and dependent corollary proceed unchanged.
issues.why_classification: From the old source, CᵀC=diag(1-b²,1), while the later calculation explicitly uses t^(-2)=1-b². These facts uniquely force the missing square root. No inference or guarantee must be replaced; this is a transcriptional exponent error.

issues.title: Wrong squared equality condition in Case A
issues.failure_explanation: The relevant step compares 1-b^2 with 1-1/n. Its equality condition is therefore b^2=1/n. For n at least 3 and b>0, the printed condition b=1/n is different from b=1/sqrt(n), so the claimed list of necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in ineq is false.
issues.overall_effect: The local characterization of equality in ineq is incorrect. The later strictness argument principally uses conditions (ii) and (iii), so this typo does not independently change the final bound or its regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change condition (i) to b²=1/n, equivalently b=1/√n because b>0. Leave the remaining equality and strictness argument unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Equality in the displayed comparison 1-b²≥1-1/n uniquely forces b²=1/n. The correction is directly recoverable from the old display, and the proof does not rely on the erroneous b=1/n condition.

issues.title: Missing converse for the equality criterion

failure_location.quote: which finalizes the proof of the equality criteria.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now let us analyze the equality case.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims both equality implies the stated clustering and the clustering implies equality. The old equality analysis establishes only the first direction: it starts from equality, derives the block structure and cluster magnitudes, and then declares the criterion finished. It never starts with an admissible three-cluster configuration and proves that the optimal smallest singular value equals 1/sqrt(n). Equal-norm collinear row clusters have identical square vectors, so the new converse addresses the same old condition.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficiency direction of the equality characterization in pr, and consequently the corresponding if-and-only-if assertion in co, is unproved. This root does not affect the inequality or the necessity direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append the omitted converse. Let x, y, and z be the common square vectors in clusters of sizes p, q, and r. Orthogonality gives px+qy+rz=0, while the prescribed magnitudes give |px|=(n+p)/(2n), |qy|=(n+q)/(2n), and |rz|=(n+r)/(2n). Applying the cosine rule to this triangle yields |x|+|y|-|x+y|=2/n, cyclically, for pairs from distinct clusters; the expression is zero within a cluster. The row-square singular-value identity therefore gives maximal smallest-singular-value squared equal to 1/n. This proves sufficiency in the proposition, and the stated polygonal correspondence transfers it to the corollary.
issues.why_classification: The missing implication is a genuine proof omission, not a typo. Nevertheless, a short local cosine-rule calculation using identities already present in the source restores the exact if-and-only-if statements in both affected results, without a new lemma, new proof architecture, or any weakening.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Considering the triangle formed by the sums of vectors of the three given clusters and applying the cosine rule, we obtain formula \eqref{blck} and thus the sufficiency of the formulated equality condition.

issues.title: Wrong middle block dimension

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $E_p$, $E_q$ and $E_r$ in the diagonal blocks are the all-ones matrices of sizes $p$, $q$ and $r$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation blck partitions M into blocks of sizes p, q, and r. Its middle diagonal block must therefore contain the q-by-q all-ones matrix E_q. The printed E_p has size p-by-p and cannot occupy that slot when p differs from q, contradicting the sentence immediately following the display.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed block decomposition used in the equality analysis is not literally well-defined for general cluster sizes, so the equality proof of pr and the dependent equality criterion in co require the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the middle diagonal block (2/(qn))E_p in the block display by (2/(qn))E_q. No other part of the equality analysis or the dependent corollary needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The middle slot is q-by-q, and the sentence immediately following the display explicitly identifies its all-ones matrix as E_q. Thus E_p is an ill-typed, uniquely correctable index transcription.

issues.title: Overstrong singular-vector lemma

failure_location.quote: their sums $v_1^2 + v_2^2$, $v_1^2 + v_3^2$ and $v_2^2 + v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear too

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, the conjugated square of the first right-singular vector is oriented as the sum of the squares of vectors $v_i$ and $v_j$.

issues.failure_explanation: Take square vectors s1=(1,0), s2=(0,1), and s3=(1,2), which are pairwise non-collinear and have real square roots under the paper's square map. Nevertheless, s1+s2=(1,1) and s1+s3=(2,2) are collinear. By the old proof's correct correspondence between a pair sum and the right-singular directions, the associated two row-pair matrices share their singular-vector directions. Thus the old all-three pairwise-distinct conclusion is false, while at least two distinct directions are guaranteed.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma le is false as stated, and its use in Case A to assert that a fixed direction occurs for at most one of three submatrices is unsupported. The weaker existence of one submatrix avoiding that direction still suffices for pr, and hence for co.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Lemma le's conclusion by the weaker statement that at least two of the three row-pair matrices have distinct first, and hence distinct second, right-singular directions. Writing s_i=v_i², if all three sums s_1+s_2, s_1+s_3, and s_2+s_3 were collinear, identities such as 2s_1=(s_1+s_2)+(s_1+s_3)-(s_2+s_3) would force all s_i to be collinear, a contradiction. In Case A, use the resulting two distinct directions to choose an equality submatrix whose smallest right-singular direction is not (±1,0)ᵀ; this still breaks condition (iii) and preserves the proposition and corollary unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample prevents preservation of the lemma's all-three pairwise-distinct conclusion, so a genuine but limited weakening of the primary formal result is necessary. The weaker lemma is recognizably comparable, has a short contained proof, and supplies exactly the downstream fact needed for Case A, avoiding both global reconstruction and any loss in the proposition or corollary.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Then at least two of the three $2 \times 2$ matrices composed of these vectors as rows have pairwise different first (and second) right-singular vectors.

issues.title: Undefined and branch-unsafe singular-vector angle formula
issues.failure_explanation: Choose three pairwise non-collinear square vectors s1=(1,0), s2=(-1,1), and s3=(0,1), each of which has a real square root under the displayed square map. For the pair s1,s2, the denominator in the old arctangent quotient is the first coordinate of s1+s2 and equals zero, while the numerator is its second coordinate and equals one. Thus the formula is undefined on an admissible lemma input. Away from zero denominators, a one-argument arctangent also fails to record the quadrant needed to distinguish the first from the second singular direction.
issues.overall_effect: The angle calculation used to justify le is not valid uniformly on its stated domain, leaving the lemma proof and its Case A use in pr incomplete; co is transitively affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let X=v_i1²-v_i2²+v_j1²-v_j2² and Y=2v_i1v_i2+2v_j1v_j2. Replace the quotient formula by 2γ=atan2(Y,X) modulo 2π, and specify that γ selects the right-singular direction for the larger singular value, with the other direction orthogonal to it. Pairwise non-collinearity ensures (X,Y)≠(0,0). This supplies a branch-safe singular-direction correspondence for the lemma and its Case A use.
issues.why_classification: The old quotient and principal arctangent require genuine branch and zero-denominator correction, so the defect is more than a transcriptional typo. The repair is nevertheless a standard, short, local eigendirection calculation that changes no hypothesis, conclusion, rate, or downstream guarantee.
